claims.text: The baseline is a nanoscale, equimolar PtPdRhRuIrOs single-phase solid-solution catalyst.
The controlled intervention is a 10–20% relative increase in Ru content, with compensating reductions in other metals.
The proposed compositional change can retain a well-mixed, single-phase solid solution.
Increasing Ru content modifies the catalyst's local electronic structure and atomic-site ensembles.
Increasing Ru content shifts the ensemble d-band center.
The Ru-induced electronic-structure change alters the binding energies of key ethanol-oxidation adsorbates.
Poisoning intermediates such as adsorbed CO are formed during ethanol oxidation on this catalyst.
The predicted d-band shift weakens adsorption of poisoning intermediates such as CO.
Weaker poison adsorption enables more facile removal through adsorption of oxygenated species and subsequent oxidation.
More facile removal of poisoning intermediates increases ethanol-oxidation turnover and activity.
More facile removal of poisoning intermediates reduces deactivation and increases catalyst durability.
Relative to the equimolar baseline, the Ru-enriched catalyst will have a lower ethanol-oxidation onset potential.
Relative to the equimolar baseline, the Ru-enriched catalyst will have higher cyclic-voltammetry peak current density.
Relative to the equimolar baseline, the Ru-enriched catalyst will show less deactivation during chronoamperometry.
The proposed effects should hold in acidic or alkaline electrolyte between 25°C and 80°C over potentials relevant to ethanol oxidation.
The proposed effects require the catalyst to remain a well-mixed, single-phase solid solution.
CO-stripping voltammetry can evaluate the proposed change in poisoning or intermediate adsorption.
XPS can identify electronic or binding-energy shifts associated with the proposed Ru-induced modulation.
